title.narrative: Water Resource Development and Livelihoods Support Project Maralal

description.narrative: This is a six (6) months project designed to specifically provide targeted beneficiaries in Samburu East and Samburu North Districts with improved access to clean drinking water and diversified livelihood options by introducing new technology for food and vegetable production. A key component in this project is the building of community assets, such as access roads through Cash for Work activities; hence opening access to the region for borehole construction as well as other essential goods and services. To improve access to clean drinking water, the project will construct and equip a borehole at Lchakwai, Samburu East to serve an estimated 2,600 community members. The community in Lchakwai was involved in the HVCA and the water project was identified as the community priority. However due to infrastructural challenges, it was not possible constructed the planned borehole Lack of access meant that the activity could not take place, and needed to be redesigned to take into account accessibility of the area. The repair of the Lchakwai access road and construction of a borehole will enable the community members’ access portable water and reduce the distance walked and time spent in search of water To diversify livelihood options, the project will promote green house farming technology among target communities. Three green houses will be provided to farmer groups and will result in two key changes; first the groups practicing green house farming will have an alternative source of income as they sell the produce and secondly there will be access to an improved and diversified diet as vegetables become available for household consumption. The green house farming is appropriate for women as they often have no means of earning a livelihood as men are primarily engaged with livestock. Women also go to markets and they identified a gap in the supply of vegetables, as many people do not engage in farming of vegetables.
